Questions:
- How does Redwood account tokens when the same "conversation id" contains calls to different model families? Is there any prefix-coalescing or does switch-to-new-model force a new billing window?
- How are minimums/rounding applied in those cases? We saw rounding that looked like it aggregated across the two calls and rounded up to a higher slab.
- If we intentionally switch to a smaller model for follow-ups (lower cost), can we avoid paying the large-context minimum from the first call?

We can share specific invoice lines if that helps (I attached the CSV). We're trying to decide whether to ask for a one-off credit or renegotiate packaging.

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the CSV, that was helpful. I pulled the invoice lines and sketched a short explanation below. Attaching a sample statement for the two calls in question (acme_sample_invoice_q2.csv).

Short answer up front: token accounting is per-request but we apply session-window aggregation and cache/coalescing rules that can change how rounding/minimums appear on the invoice. Model switches affect whether the runtime can reuse KV/prefix state. When the runtime cannot reuse prefix state (different model family or incompatible quantization), we treat the next call as a new hot-start for caching but we still run our billing aggregation step which groups requests that fall into the same "active window" for a customer session. That grouping is what created the larger billed slab you saw.

More detail and examples:
- Per-request tokens: each API call reports raw input+output token counts.
- Active-window aggregation: we group requests from the same conversation id within a short inactivity window (default 10s) and aggregate tokens for rounding/minimums at aggregation time so customers aren't charged per-microcall.
- Model-family boundary: if a call switches to a different model family (e.g., model-a -> model-b with incompatible runtime path), KV/prefix reuse is disabled; that affects latency and cache credits but does NOT automatically reset the aggregation window. Aggregation is based on activity, not model family.
- Rounding/minimums: aggregation buckets are rounded according to the billing quantum in your agreement (example: invoice lines are rounded up to the nearest 100-token slab for per-call items and then packaged against any committed units). This can make two short calls look like a single rounded slab if they fall in the same active window.

Implication for your use case:
- If you want to guarantee a follow-up uses a cheaper per-token rate (and avoid the large-context slab), you can either: 1) emit the follow-up in a new conversation id (breaks aggregation), or 2) wait out the inactivity window before calling the smaller model so aggregation doesn't combine the calls.
- We can also adjust the active-window timeout at contract-level for high-volume customers; setting it lower reduces accidental coalescing but increases per-call billing granularity.

If you'd like, I can:
- Produce a redline of the two invoice lines showing the raw tokens vs. the aggregated billed slab,
- Ask our pricing team for a temporary credit if the aggregation produced an unexpected single large slab on your first month after testing, or
- Discuss a packaging change (hybrid-context add-on) that treats model-family fallbacks more conservatively for aggregation.

Which would you prefer?
